item.stem:
Draw the line of symmetry on this shape.

[Image: an elongated kite shape figure with two pointy-ends at either end.]

descriptors:

[Image: an elongated kite shape figure with two pointy ends at either end. A dotted line goes lengthwise through the figure, through the pointy ends.]

item.figure_description: A quadrilateral kite shape oriented diagonally on a blank background. It has a sharp, acute vertex pointing toward the bottom left. From this vertex, two long straight sides of equal length extend upward and to the right: one side goes steeply up and right to an upper vertex, and the other side goes gently up and right to a lower-right vertex. The top side is a short horizontal segment extending rightward from the upper vertex, and the right side is a short vertical segment extending upward from the lower-right vertex, meeting at a top-right corner.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Jay has to draw a shape.
- It must have 5 sides.
- It must have one line of symmetry.
Jay has started to draw the shape.
Complete Jay’s shape.

[Image: an incomplete shape with three sides forming a rectangle on a grid.]

descriptors:
Correct shape drawn which has 5 sides and 1 line of symmetry. The new vertex must be within ±2 mm of the line of symmetry (accept the new vertex anywhere on the line of symmetry, provided there are 5 sides).
[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. Two lines drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.] OR
[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. Two lines sloping inwards are drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.]

[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. The rectangle is completed with a fourth line and then two additional lines are drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.]
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description: A 10 by 10 square grid. A three-sided incomplete shape is drawn with thick black lines along the grid lines: a horizontal bottom segment 6 units long (leaving 2 units of margin on the left and 2 units on the right along the bottom edge of the grid), and two vertical segments each 4 units tall rising upward from the two ends of the bottom segment (leaving 6 units of grid space above them). The top of the shape is open.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
An 8 by 8 grid of square cells with a vertical dashed line of symmetry running along the central vertical grid line (between the 4th and 5th columns from the left).
To the right of the dashed line is a six-sided polygon with vertices at grid intersections (with column lines 0 to 8 from left to right, and row lines 0 to 8 from top to bottom):
- (column 4, row 3) on the dashed line
- (column 5, row 2)
- (column 6, row 4)
- (column 7, row 4)
- (column 7, row 6)
- (column 4, row 5) on the dashed line

The edges of the polygon connect these vertices in sequence:
- A straight segment from (4, 3) up and right to (5, 2)
- A segment from (5, 2) down and right to (6, 4)
- A horizontal segment from (6, 4) to (7, 4)
- A vertical segment from (7, 4) down to (7, 6)
- A slanted segment from (7, 6) up and left to (4, 5)
- A vertical segment of length 2 along the dashed line from (4, 5) up to (4, 3)
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: In which of the following figures is the dotted line a line of symmetry?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a square into two opposite trapezoids.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a rectangle into two opposite right angle triangles.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a pentagon into a trapezoid and an irregular pentagon.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a hexagon in the middle.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four geometric shapes, each intersected by a dotted line:
- Option A shows a square with a tilted dotted line that enters through the top side near the top-left corner and exits through the bottom side near the bottom-right corner, dividing the square into two non-congruent trapezoids.
- Option B shows a horizontal rectangle with a dotted line running along the diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner.
- Option C shows a regular pentagon with one vertex at the top and a horizontal base at the bottom. A slightly slanted, nearly horizontal dotted line cuts through the left and right sides below the center, dividing it into an upper portion and a lower trapezoid.
- Option D shows a regular hexagon with horizontal top and bottom edges. A vertical dotted line passes through the exact center, bisecting the top and bottom edges into two identical mirror-image halves.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: In which of these drawings is the dotted line a line of symmetry?

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Outline of a human body with a dotted line]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four line drawings labeled A, B, C, and D, each with a straight dotted line:
- A: A top-down view of a butterfly, tilted diagonally. The dotted line passes straight through the body from between the antennae to the tail, splitting the butterfly into two symmetric halves.
- B: A front-facing outline of a human body standing upright with arms at the sides. A horizontal dotted line passes across the waist.
- C: A front view of an elephant with its trunk curved slightly to one side, its tail visible on only one side, and asymmetric feet. A vertical dotted line runs down the center of the drawing.
- D: A snake drawn horizontally, stretched out with its head on the right and tail on the left. A vertical dotted line cuts across the snake's body near the middle.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: a complex figure shaped like a bow tie with lines of symmetry shaded on faded square lines.]

How many lines of symmetry does this figure have?
reference_items.figure_description:
A shaded, symmetric bow-tie-shaped polygon is drawn on a grid of squares measuring 6 columns wide and 4 rows high.
- The shape has two vertical outer ends: a left vertical side along the first interior vertical grid line spanning the middle 2 units in height, and an identical right vertical side along the fifth vertical grid line spanning the middle 2 units in height.
- From the top and bottom endpoints of each vertical side, the top and bottom edges slope inward toward a narrower central "neck."
- At the center of the figure, the top and bottom boundaries each form a short horizontal segment parallel to the grid lines.
- The figure is horizontally and vertically symmetric across the central vertical grid line and the central horizontal grid line.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
A square grid 6 units wide and 6 units tall. A vertical dashed line labeled "m" at the bottom divides the grid vertically down the center (3 units from the left edge and 3 units from the right edge). On the left side of line m, a right triangle is drawn along the grid lines with vertices at:
- 2 units from the left edge and 2 units above the bottom edge (the right-angled vertex, located 1 unit to the left of line m)
- 1 unit from the left edge and 2 units above the bottom edge (located 2 units to the left of line m)
- 2 units from the left edge and 5 units above the bottom edge (1 unit below the top edge, located 1 unit to the left of line m).
The vertical leg of the triangle is 3 units long and lies along the grid line 1 unit to the left of line m; the horizontal base is 1 unit long and lies 2 units above the bottom edge.

reference_items.figure_description:
A grid measuring 8 squares wide and 6 squares high. At the bottom right of the grid, a single square cell is indicated with dimension arrows showing a width of '1 cm' and a height of '1 cm'. An incomplete polygon is drawn with heavy black lines on the grid intersections:
- A horizontal segment 4 units long on the 1st horizontal line from the top, extending from column 1 to column 5 (where grid lines are numbered 0 to 8 horizontally, and 0 to 6 vertically).
- From the point (1, 1), a diagonal segment runs down and right 2 units horizontally and 2 units vertically to (3, 3).
- From (3, 3), a vertical segment runs down 2 units to (3, 5).
- From (3, 5), a horizontal segment runs right 2 units to (5, 5).
The points (5, 1) and (5, 5) are currently open endpoints.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
